content: DLG1, also referred to as synapse-associated protein 97 (SAP97), is a scaffold protein encoded by the SAP97 gene in humans. It belongs to the mammalian MAGUK (membrane-associated guanylate kinase) protein family and shares similarity with the Drosophila protein Dlg1. In humans, the protein is sometimes called hDlg1, while the gene is named DLG1. SAP97 is expressed in epithelial cells throughout the body, including in the kidney and brain. In the brain, it plays a role in the trafficking of ionotropic receptors from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to the plasma membrane. It may also be involved in the trafficking of AMPA receptors (AMPAR) during synaptic plasticity. SAP97 has been shown to regulate cell-to-cell adhesion during cell death and may interact with human papillomavirus (HPV). Its function in the brain involves the trafficking of transmembrane receptors from the ER to the plasma membrane. Experimental studies have investigated SAP97's function by either knocking out its expression or overexpressing it heterologously. Mice with a knockout of the SAP97 gene die perinatally, exhibit cleft palate, and have renal function deficiencies. Overexpression of SAP97 in mammalian neurons has been found to increase synaptic strength. Mutations in the DLG1 gene have been associated with Crohn's disease. The protein structure of SAP97 includes an alternatively spliced N-terminal domain, three PDZ domains, an SH3 domain, a hook domain, an I3 domain, and an inactive guanylate kinase (GK) domain. Each of these domains interacts with specific partners, contributing to SAP97's unique functions. The N-terminal domain can be alternatively spliced to include either a double-cysteine/palmitoylation site (α-isoform) or an L27 domain (β-isoform). The L27 domain facilitates oligomerization of SAP97 with other SAP97 molecules, CASK, and other L27-domain-containing proteins. Additionally, there is a myosin VI binding site near the N-terminal, which may play a role in the internalization of AMPAR. Each of SAP97's PDZ domains has distinct binding partners. For example, the first PDZ domain binds to the AMPAR subunit GluR1, while the last PDZ domain interacts with neuroligin. The GK domain enables SAP97 to bind to GKAP/SAPAP-family proteins.
